h1: The 6 Best Privacy Screens for HP Monitors, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best HP Monitor Privacy Screens: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 privacy screen filters that fit HP monitors in 22, 24 and 27 inch sizes, scored on fit, pack size, mounting and viewing angle.
summary: The IPROKKO 24 inch 2-pack is the pick for most HP monitors, since it matches the common 24 inch, 16:9 panel and names HP compatibility in its listing. The Magicmoon and Peslv 2-packs are close alternatives for the same size, the 27 inch pack adds blue-light reduction, and the Vxaop is the one for older 16:10 HP panels.
intro: Privacy screens are sold by diagonal size, and that is the trap. Two HP monitors can both be called 24 inch and still need different filters, because one has a 16:9 panel and the other a 16:10 panel with a taller picture. A filter cut for the wrong ratio leaves a strip uncovered at the bottom or overhangs the bezel, and either way it fails at the one job it exists to do. Before you shop for a brand, check the aspect ratio of your actual monitor.

This ranking sorts six privacy filters sold for HP monitor sizes by how closely they match the common HP panels. We reviewed the listings for diagonal size, aspect ratio, pack count, mounting style and any extras such as blue-light filtering. Most listings state little beyond these basics, so we do not quote viewing angles or light loss that they do not give. None of these is HP-branded, so compatibility rests on size and ratio.

products.name: IPROKKO [2-Pack] 24 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 16:9 Widescreen Monitor
products.verdict: A 24 inch, 16:9 two-pack that explicitly lists HP compatibility.
products.description:
The IPROKKO is a pack of two privacy filters for 24 inch, 16:9 widescreen monitors, and its listing mentions HP compatibility. It costs between $25 and $50.

It ranks first because a 24 inch, 16:9 panel is by far the most common size on office HP monitors, and this is the filter whose listing names the brand. That small detail does not guarantee a fit, but it shows the seller checked the product against HP panels. The two-pack is useful in practice, since many desks run a pair of monitors, or you may want a spare for the day a filter gets scratched. It sits above the other 24 inch packs only because of the explicit HP mention.

Buy it if you have a standard 24 inch HP monitor and want a matched pair. Measure the visible screen width and height first, because the filter has to cover the whole picture area.
pros: Two filters for a dual setup
Low price bracket for a pair
cons: Fit still depends on exact size
products.idealFor: Buyers with a standard 24 inch, 16:9 HP monitor who want an explicit brand mention.
products.skipIf: Your HP monitor is 16:10 or a different size.

products.name: Magicmoon 2-Pack 24 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 16:9 Monitor
products.verdict: A second 24 inch, 16:9 pack at a similar price, for buyers who want a choice.
products.description:
The Magicmoon is a 2-pack privacy filter sized for 24 inch, 16:9 monitors. The listing gives little else beyond the size, ratio and pack count, and it costs between $25 and $50.

It takes second place because it matches the IPROKKO on size, ratio, pack count and price, and loses only on the brand mention. If your HP monitor is a standard 24 inch panel, this is a reasonable second choice, and you may find one in stock when the other is not. The listing's lack of detail means you should plan to measure carefully and be ready to return it if the fit is off.

Choose it when the IPROKKO is unavailable or you prefer this seller's return terms. Do not buy it for a 16:10 or non-standard HP panel.
pros: Same price band as the leader
products.idealFor: Buyers comparing alternative 24 inch 2-packs at a similar price point.
products.skipIf: You want an explicit HP compatibility statement.

products.name: Peslv [2-Pack] 24 Inch Privacy Screen for Computer Monitor, 16:9 Aspect Ratio
products.verdict: A removable 24 inch, 16:9 two-pack that is easy to take off for presentations.
products.description:
The Peslv pack contains two removable 24 inch, 16:9 privacy screens. It sits in the $50 to $100 price band, higher than the other 24 inch packs.

It ranks third because removability is the one feature it states that the others leave unclear. A removable filter lets you take it off for a team review or a presentation, so colleagues are not squinting at your screen from the side, and put it back afterward. That flexibility has a cost, since filters that attach with tabs or adhesive strips can leave the screen edge looking less neat than a permanent fit. It also costs more than the IPROKKO and Magicmoon without adding a stated spec.

Pick it if your workday swings between private work and shared screens. If you rarely remove a filter, buy one of the cheaper packs.
products.idealFor: Workers who switch between private tasks and shared presentations.
products.skipIf: You never need to take the filter off.

products.name: [2 Pack] 27 Inch Computer Monitor Privacy Screen, Blue Light Filter
products.verdict: A 27 inch, 16:9 pair with blue-light filtering built into the film.
products.description:
This pack holds two 27 inch, 16:9 privacy screens that also filter blue light. It costs between $25 and $50.

It ranks fourth only because 27 inch HP monitors are less common than 24 inch ones in offices. For those who do own one, the pack is good value for a pair, and the blue-light feature is a bonus, not a core function. Blue-light films tint the picture slightly warmer, which some people like for evening work and others dislike for color-sensitive tasks. Privacy filters also darken the image, so a 27 inch panel with limited brightness may look dim.

Buy it for a 27 inch HP display used for general office work and long hours. Skip it if you edit photos or video, where the color tint can interfere.
products.idealFor: Buyers with a 27 inch HP monitor who also want blue-light reduction.
products.skipIf: You do color-critical photo or video work.

products.name: Vxaop [2-Pack] 22 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter (16:10 Aspect Ratio)
products.verdict: A 22 inch, 16:10 pair for older or compact HP monitors with a taller picture.
products.description:
The Vxaop pack contains two 22 inch privacy filters cut for a 16:10 aspect ratio. It costs between $25 and $50.

It ranks fifth because it serves a narrower group. Many older HP monitors from the late 2000s and early 2010s used 16:10 panels, which are slightly taller than modern 16:9 screens, and a standard 22 inch 16:9 filter would not cover them. This pack fixes that. If your monitor is a 22 inch 16:9 panel, though, this is the wrong shape, so check the ratio before you buy. Without further detail on the listing, the fit rests on measurement.

Choose it if you own an older HP monitor and measure a taller-than-usual picture area. For newer HP screens, one of the 24 inch packs is the better match.
products.idealFor: Buyers with an older or compact HP monitor that uses a 16:10 aspect ratio instead of 16:9.
products.skipIf: Your HP monitor has a 16:9 panel.

products.name: Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 24 Inch 16:9 Aspect Ratio Monitor
products.verdict: A single 24 inch, 16:9 filter for trying the idea on one monitor first.
products.description:
This is a single privacy screen filter for a 24 inch, 16:9 monitor. It costs between $25 and $50 and the listing gives no further details.

It ranks last because the two-packs offer more for a similar price. One filter is enough if you have a single HP monitor and want to see whether you like the tradeoffs, which include a dimmer picture and a narrower viewing angle. With no mention of HP or removability, and no brand to speak of, it is a low-information purchase.

Buy it if you have one monitor and are not yet sure a privacy filter is for you. If you have two monitors, a pack costs about the same.
pros: Single filter to try the idea
cons: No HP mention or other details
products.idealFor: Budget-focused buyers who want to try a privacy filter on a single HP monitor first.

whatMatters.detail: Aspect ratio is the width to height proportion of the panel, and 16:9 is the modern default while 16:10 is taller. A filter cut for the wrong ratio will leave a strip uncovered or hang off the bezel. Check your monitor's spec sheet or measure the visible screen, and match the ratio on the listing.

Size is the diagonal of the visible screen, usually printed as 22, 24 or 27 inches. A filter that is a few millimeters too small leaves a visible gap, and one that is too large will not seat. Measure width and height of the display area and compare them to the listing's dimensions.

A privacy filter darkens the screen when seen from the side, typically beyond about 30 degrees, using tiny louvers. Narrower angles give more privacy but a tighter sweet spot for you. Look for a stated angle in the listing, and be cautious when none is given.

Filters attach by adhesive strips, tabs that hook the bezel, or clips. Strips hold well but are harder to remove, while tabs let you take the filter off for presentations. Check which method the listing describes before you buy.

Every privacy filter absorbs some light, so the picture looks dimmer, and blue-light variants add a warm tint. Turn up the monitor brightness to compensate. If color accuracy matters, choose a plain filter without blue-light film.

faq.q: Will these fit every HP monitor?
faq.a: They fit by size and ratio, not by brand. Check your monitor's diagonal and whether it is 16:9 or 16:10, then match the listing. A close but wrong ratio will not cover the whole screen.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with privacy filters?
faq.a: Ordering by diagonal only. Two 24 inch screens can have different shapes, and a few millimeters of mismatch shows. Measure the visible area before you buy.

faq.q: Is a privacy filter worth it over turning my screen?
faq.a: It is if you work in a shared space, such as an open office or a cafe. Angling the screen is free but unreliable. A filter keeps working when you move or someone walks behind you.

faq.q: How do I install one without bubbles?
faq.a: Clean the screen with a microfiber cloth, align the filter's top edge, and attach the tabs or strips slowly. Do not press on the filter surface. Check it is the right way around, since some have a glossy and matte side.

faq.q: Will it make the screen too dark?
faq.a: It will dim the picture because it blocks light at angles and absorbs some head-on too. Raising the monitor brightness helps. If the screen is already dim, this can be a problem.
Wipe gently with a dry microfiber cloth, or a slightly damp one for smudges. Avoid sprays and harsh chemicals, which can mar the coating. Store removable filters flat in a sleeve.

finalTake: For most HP desks, the IPROKKO 24 Inch two-pack is the best privacy screen to buy, since it matches the most common size and names HP compatibility. The Magicmoon is a close alternative. Choose the Peslv for removability, the 27 inch pack for larger panels with blue-light filtering, and the Vxaop only if you measure a 16:10 screen.
